evidence.claim: On a healthy hooks.json the probe reports FIRED only when (1) the hook process writes HOOK_FIRED:<nonce>:<id> after a real PreToolUse trigger and (2) the client inventory document lists that same hook as loaded. The two writers are the hook script and the loader; file presence is not either signal.

The same probe against a config that adds an unknown top-level $schema key (the Codex zero-load precedent) reports NOT-FIRED: inventory empty, trigger_count 0, sentinel absent. Every hook file remains on disk.

A filesystem-only checker that treats hooks.json plus scripts/*.py as FIRED is fooled by the broken fixture (verdict FIRED) while the real probe reports NOT-FIRED. The probe therefore cannot pass on filesystem evidence alone.

failure_class_seeded: plugin appears installed but hooks are unloaded

implementation.load_rule: Any top-level key outside {hooks}, including $schema, loads ZERO hooks (Codex-shaped inventory). Trigger then runs nothing.

negative_controls.description: Unknown top-level $schema key: client loads zero hooks; probe NOT-FIRED
Filesystem-only anti-pattern is fooled; real probe is not
negative_controls.good_state_output: real probe FIRED on healthy (discriminates, not silent both)
